title: Slotted points
prompt:
Implement `class Point` with `__slots__ = ('x', 'y')`:

- constructor takes x, y
- instances must NOT support arbitrary attributes (`p.z = 1` raises `AttributeError`)
- `__eq__`/`__hash__` consistent: equal points share a hash (define both)
- `distance_to(other)` returns the Euclidean distance (use math.hypot)
boilerplate:
import math

class Point:
    __slots__ = ('x', 'y')

    # TODO: __init__, __eq__, __hash__, distance_to

tests.name: slots enforce the shape
tests.hint: __slots__ removes the per-instance __dict__ — that is the point.

tests.name: eq/hash/distance
tests.code:
assert Point(1, 2) == Point(1, 2)
assert hash(Point(1, 2)) == hash(Point(1, 2))
assert Point(1, 2) != Point(2, 1)
assert abs(Point(0, 0).distance_to(Point(3, 4)) - 5.0) < 1e-9
assert hash(Point(1, 2)) in {hash(Point(1, 2))}
print('ok')
tests.hint: Define __eq__ and __hash__ together (tuple hash of the coordinates).
